claims.text: envs/staging and envs/production each hold a full set of manifests (api, migration hook, database, other services); apart from line-1 header comments and staging's encrypted Secrets they differ only in api replicas (2 vs 3) and the api and migrate image tags.
Only staging's folder holds Secrets, encrypted by scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh, which writes sealed-<name>.yaml into envs/staging only; envs/production has none.

claims.text: The promotion commit sets production's api and migrate tags to staging's (1.0.0), changing api.yaml and migrate-hook.yaml one line each, and builds nothing. A second run changes nothing; git commit with nothing to commit exits non-zero, so the script stops after the promote line.

claims.text: 1.0.0 is the image CI pushed to ghcr.io (the container registry) under a sha- tag, pushed again as 1.0.0 by the release workflow without a rebuild, and the tag Argo CD synced on staging.
Protection rules on a GitHub deployment environment, such as required reviewers, must pass before a job that references the environment starts; CI's staging job references environment staging.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Actions docs: Managing environments for deployment > Deployment protection rules; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 .github/workflows/ci.yml:158-162

claims.text: When the team wants production to change only after a second person has looked, open the promotion commit as a pull request so review and required checks decide when production changes, instead of pushing to main.

With a full copy of the manifests per environment, a change meant for both (e.g. a new probe) must be made in both folders; a change made in only one leaves the environments different without anyone choosing it.
In the lab nothing syncs production: OpenTofu only plans the production cluster, and no Application in namespace argocd has source.path envs/production (script prints 'none').
claims.source_hint: gitops-promote.sh:30-34 @ stage-3; output lines 42-43; DECISIONS.md §3 outline devops/iac (production chỉ plan); scripts/devops/tofu-environments.sh

claims.text: gitops-promote.sh: 9 tag_in reads the api tag; 13 diffs the folders, dropping diff lines whose comment starts at column 1 (the header comments); 20-21 read both tags; 23-24 replace the tag in api.yaml and migrate-hook.yaml; 25 config_commit commits; 26-27 show stat and diff.

An Application applies the manifests of the folder its source names; staging's reads envs/staging, so at work production's Argo CD would sync envs/production from main after the merge, and a folder shared by two clusters' Argo CD would send every commit to both.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Declarative Setup > Applications (spec.source.path); deploy/gitops/config-repo/apps/staging.yaml @ stage-3

claims.text: Merging a branch brings every change on it that the target lacks, including values meant to stay different between environments.
A branch per environment can work when environments differ only in how far behind each other they are; one folder per environment on main fits when environments must differ for good (replicas, tags).
claims.source_hint: Outline misconception 2; DECISIONS.md §3 outline devops/gitops item (6)

claims.text: Building the image again, even from the same commit, makes a new image staging never ran: what the build pulls in can differ, such as a newer image behind the base tag in FROM, and its digest can differ from staging's.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Build best practices (Pin base image versions; Rebuild your images often)

claims.text: A tag is a mutable reference: if another image is pushed under the same tag, Pods pulling that tag can get different code; an image digest identifies one specific image. So naming 1.0.0 gives staging's image only while nobody re-pushes 1.0.0.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Concepts > Containers > Images (Image names; image digest)
